title: 2027 Hoover Fellows Program at Stanford University
summary: The Hoover Institution at Stanford University is seeking outstanding early-career scholars for the 2027 Hoover Fellows Program , an opportunity for researchers whose work has implications for public policy. Hoover Fellows will be based at the Hoover Institution in Stanford, California , where they will have the opportunity to pursue scholarly research, publish academic work, and contribute to the intellectual life of one of Stanford University s leading research centers. The fellowship is particularly suited to scholars working in fields such as economics, history, international relations, national security, political science, and public policy. According to the 2027 opportunity information provided by the Hoover Institution, appointments are for one to three years , and the position carries no teaching responsibilities . About the Hoover Fellows Program The Hoover Institution is a research center at Stanford University focused on research and scholarship with relevance to public policy. Hoover scholars contribute to research and intellectual discussions on issues including economics, national security, international relations, and governance. The Hoover Fellows Program provides early-career scholars with an opportunity to concentrate on their research and scholarly writing while participating in the intellectual community at Hoover and engaging with Stanford s broader research environment. During the fellowship, Fellows are expected to produce scholarly articles and books that have implications for public policy. They are also expected to contribute to the intellectual life of the Hoover Institution. Unlike some academic fellowships, the position does not include teaching responsibilities, allowing Fellows to focus primarily on research and publication. Fellowship Benefits The 2027 Hoover Fellow position offers a highly competitive compensation package. Salary Selected Fellows will receive a 12-month base salary ranging from $169,950 to $230,000 . Housing Allowance In addition to the base salary, Fellows will receive a $20,000 annual housing allowance . Research Environment Fellows will be based at the Hoover Institution on Stanford University s campus in Stanford, California. They will also be encouraged to engage with Stanford s wider research community in their respective fields. This provides Fellows with an opportunity to interact with scholars and researchers beyond Hoover while developing their own academic research agendas. Fellowship Duration The 2027 opportunity specifies an appointment term of one to three years . The position is based at the Hoover Institution, Stanford, California , and Fellows are expected to participate in the Institution s intellectual community while pursuing their research. Areas of Research The Hoover Fellows Program is open to scholars working in relevant academic and policy fields. Examples of eligible fields include: Economics History International Relations National Security Political Science Public Policy Applicants from related disciplines may also be considered where their research aligns with the Hoover Institution s mission and has meaningful implications for public policy. Eligibility Requirements Applicants must be early-career scholars who hold a Ph.D. or equivalent degree in a relevant field , or who expect to complete the degree by September 1, 2027 . The opportunity is therefore particularly relevant to doctoral candidates approaching completion of their Ph.D. as well as scholars who have already completed their doctoral studies. Applicants should have an academic and research background that demonstrates their potential to produce significant scholarly work. Candidates are expected to show how their research can contribute to broader discussions relevant to public policy. What Will Hoover Fellows Do? Selected Fellows will primarily focus on research and scholarly activities. During the fellowship, they are expected to: Conduct research in their area of specialization. Produce scholarly articles and other academic publications. Develop books or book-length research where appropriate. Pursue research projects with implications for public policy. Contribute to the intellectual life of the Hoover Institution. Engage with Stanford s broader research community. Participate in scholarly discussions connected to their research interests. Because the position carries no teaching responsibilities , Fellows can devote their time primarily to research, writing, and intellectual engagement. Application Requirements Applicants must submit several documents as part of their application. 1. Cover Letter or Statement of Interest Applicants should provide a cover letter or statement of interest describing their academic background and experience. This document should clearly communicate the applicant s research interests, academic preparation, and reasons for seeking the Hoover Fellowship. 2. Recent Scholarly Work Applicants must submit one or more recent publications, working papers, or draft book chapters . These materials allow the selection committee to assess the applicant s research quality, scholarly writing, and potential for future contributions. 3. Curriculum Vitae Applicants must provide an up-to-date CV outlining their academic background, research experience, publications, professional experience, awards, and other relevant achievements. 4. Future Research Statement Applicants must submit a statement describing their future research plans . The research statement must be no more than two pages and should clearly explain the research the applicant intends to pursue during the fellowship and its potential significance. 5. Three Letters of Recommendation Applicants are required to provide three letters of recommendation . The letters should address the candidate s research accomplishments and potential for future research. Applicants should therefore select recommenders who can provide meaningful assessments of their academic and research capabilities. Who Should Apply? The fellowship is particularly suitable for early-career researchers who are developing independent research programmes and want to work in a leading research environment. Potential applicants include: Ph.D. candidates nearing completion of their degrees. Recent Ph.D. graduates. Early-career scholars in economics and related disciplines. Researchers working on international relations and national security. Political scientists and historians. Public policy researchers. Scholars whose research has clear implications for public policy. Applicants should have a strong research profile and be prepared to demonstrate their potential for future scholarly contributions. Location The Hoover Fellows Program is based at: Hoover Institution Stanford University Stanford, California, USA The Hoover Institution is located in the heart of Stanford University s campus, providing Fellows with access to a broader academic and research environment. Application Deadline The deadline for the 2027 Hoover Fellows Program is: November 17, 2026 Time: 11:59 PM Pacific Time Applicants are encouraged to prepare their application materials well in advance of the deadline, particularly because the application requires three recommendation letters and several research documents. How to Apply Applications must be submitted online through the Hoover Institution s application platform. Application Portal: Apply for the 2027 Hoover Fellows Program Applicants should ensure that all required documents and recommendation letters are submitted according to the instructions before the deadline. For questions about the fellowship, applicants can contact hooverfellowship@stanford.edu . The Hoover Institution notes that this inbox is checked only periodically. Important Information for Applicants Before submitting an application, prospective candidates should make sure they: Hold a Ph.D. or equivalent degree, or expect to complete it by September 1, 2027. Have a research background in a relevant academic field. Prepare a strong cover letter or statement of interest. Include recent scholarly work, working papers, or a draft book chapter. Prepare an updated academic CV. Develop a focused future research statement of no more than two pages. Identify three appropriate referees. Allow enough time for recommendation letters to be submitted. Submit the complete application before November 17, 2026, at 11:59 PM PT. Why Consider the Hoover Fellowship? For early-career scholars, the fellowship provides an opportunity to dedicate substantial time to research and scholarly publication while becoming part of the intellectual community at the Hoover Institution. The combination of a competitive salary, housing allowance, research-focused responsibilities, and access to Stanford s broader scholarly environment makes the opportunity particularly attractive to researchers seeking to advance an academic or policy-oriented career. The fellowship can also provide a valuable platform for scholars whose research seeks to connect academic scholarship with important public policy questions. Conclusion The 2027 Hoover Fellows Program at Stanford University offers an exciting opportunity for early-career scholars to pursue research in a prestigious academic and policy research environment. Successful Fellows will be expected to produce high-quality scholarly work, contribute to the intellectual life of the Hoover Institution, and engage with Stanford s wider research community. The position offers a 12-month base salary of $169,950 to $230,000 , plus a $20,000 annual housing allowance , and carries no teaching responsibilities. Researchers in economics, history, international relations, national security, political science, public policy, and related fields who meet the doctoral degree requirement are encouraged to consider applying. title: Linus Pauling Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027 at PNNL | Fully Funded Research Fellowship in the USA
summary: The Linus Pauling Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027 at the Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) is now accepting applications from outstanding early-career scientists and engineers who are ready to pursue ambitious, independent research. The prestigious fellowship provides selected researchers with full funding to undertake a major research project of their own conception at PNNL. Fellows have the opportunity to develop original research ideas, work with internationally recognised scientists, access advanced research capabilities, and contribute to discoveries addressing important scientific and national challenges. The programme is designed for the next generation of scientists and engineers who want to push the boundaries of research and development and produce work with the potential for world-recognised impact. What Is the Linus Pauling Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellowship? The Linus Pauling Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellowship is a postdoctoral research programme hosted by Pacific Northwest National Laboratory. Named after renowned scientist Linus Pauling , the fellowship supports exceptional recent and upcoming PhD graduates in science and engineering. Unlike a conventional postdoctoral position where researchers may primarily work on an established project, the Linus Pauling Fellowship allows successful candidates to propose and pursue a major research project of their own design . Applicants are expected to develop a detailed and original research proposal explaining their research plans, objectives, methodology, and anticipated outcomes. The fellowship therefore provides an opportunity for talented early-career researchers to demonstrate scientific independence while benefiting from PNNL s research environment and expertise. What Does the Fellowship Offer? Selected Linus Pauling Fellows receive full funding to pursue their proposed research at PNNL. The fellowship provides researchers with an opportunity to: Develop and conduct a major research project of their own conception. Work alongside internationally recognised researchers. Access state-of-the-art scientific and technological capabilities. Develop innovative approaches to complex research questions. Advance scientific knowledge in their chosen field. Contribute to research addressing pressing national concerns. Build their scientific and professional networks. Develop their independence as researchers. Work within one of the United States leading national laboratory environments. The programme is particularly suited to researchers who already have a strong research background and a clear vision for an ambitious postdoctoral project. Research Areas Applicants can propose research connected to PNNL s mission areas. The fellowship highlights four broad areas of research: 1. Scientific Discovery Researchers interested in fundamental and applied scientific discovery can develop projects aimed at expanding knowledge and creating new scientific capabilities. Projects may involve emerging scientific questions and approaches capable of generating significant discoveries. 2. Energy Resiliency Energy is one of PNNL s major research areas. Researchers can explore topics related to energy systems, energy technologies, resilience, sustainability, and other challenges associated with securing and transforming energy systems. 3. Data Science and Computing The fellowship also supports research involving data science and computing. This area can be relevant to researchers developing advanced computational methods, data-driven approaches, modelling techniques, artificial intelligence applications, and other computational research aligned with PNNL s mission. 4. National Security PNNL conducts research addressing important national security challenges. Applicants whose research interests align with this area may develop proposals addressing scientific and technological challenges relevant to national security. Who Can Apply? The fellowship is intended for qualified recent and upcoming PhD graduates in science and engineering . Applicants must have completed, or be on track to complete, a PhD in a science or engineering field related to the mission areas of PNNL. The degree must be from an accredited college or university . For the 2027 fellowship, qualified candidates must have completed their PhD within the last three years or prior to the start of the fellowship . This makes the opportunity particularly suitable for early-career researchers who have recently completed doctoral studies or are approaching completion. International Applicants The fellowship is based at PNNL in the United States. Applicants should note that all PNNL staff must be able to demonstrate the legal right to work in the United States . Therefore, prospective international applicants should carefully review the employment and work-authorisation requirements before applying. Eligibility should not be assumed solely based on academic qualifications. What Makes the Fellowship Competitive? The Linus Pauling Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellowship is designed for researchers who can demonstrate the potential to make significant contributions to science and engineering. A strong application should therefore go beyond simply describing an existing research project. Applicants are expected to present an original research proposal that demonstrates: A clear and important research question. Strong scientific reasoning. Originality and innovation. A well-defined research approach. Potential scientific or technological impact. Alignment with PNNL s mission areas. Clear anticipated outcomes. The potential to advance research beyond existing approaches. The ability to demonstrate an independent research vision is an important aspect of the fellowship. Research Proposal One of the central components of the application is the research proposal. Applicants must submit a detailed proposal describing the research project they intend to undertake. The proposal should communicate the central research idea clearly and explain how the proposed work could contribute to scientific or technological advancement. Candidates should carefully consider the connection between their proposed research and PNNL s research priorities. Because the fellowship allows researchers to pursue projects of their own conception, applicants should use the proposal to demonstrate both their scientific expertise and their capacity for independent research. Mentoring and Research Environment Linus Pauling Fellows benefit from mentoring by internationally recognised researchers at PNNL. This provides fellows with the opportunity to work in an environment where they can receive guidance while developing their own research programme. The fellowship combines independent research with access to experienced scientists and advanced research infrastructure. This can be particularly valuable for researchers seeking to transition from doctoral research into more independent scientific leadership. About Pacific Northwest National Laboratory Pacific Northwest National Laboratory (PNNL) is a U.S. national laboratory known for research and technological innovation in areas including energy, environment, science, and national security. PNNL conducts multidisciplinary research aimed at addressing complex scientific and societal challenges. The laboratory s research environment gives fellows the opportunity to work with researchers from different scientific and engineering disciplines and use advanced capabilities to pursue ambitious projects. Why Apply for the Linus Pauling Fellowship? The fellowship can be an important opportunity for researchers who want to establish themselves as independent scientists or engineers. Rather than simply joining an existing research programme, successful candidates can develop a significant research project based on their own scientific vision. The fellowship can help researchers: Strengthen their independent research profile. Develop a major original research project. Work with leading scientists. Access advanced laboratory capabilities. Expand their professional network. Gain experience conducting research in a national laboratory. Build a foundation for a long-term scientific career. Contribute to research with potential global impact. Application Deadline Applications for the 2027 Linus Pauling Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellowship are open until: 15 October 2026 at 4:00 p.m. Pacific Standard Time (PST). Applicants should ensure that their complete application is submitted before the stated deadline. How to Apply Interested candidates should apply through the official PNNL careers portal. Application Link: https://careers.pnnl.gov/jobs/11983?lang=en-us Applicants should review the official vacancy and fellowship information carefully for the complete application requirements, required documents, and current instructions. The official fellowship page is also available through PNNL: https://www.pnnl.gov/projects/linus-pauling-distinguished-postdoctoral-fellowship Tips for Preparing a Strong Application Because the fellowship is designed for researchers with the potential to generate world-recognised discoveries, applicants should dedicate significant attention to their research proposal. Develop an Original Research Idea The project should demonstrate originality and address a meaningful scientific or technological question. Demonstrate Alignment With PNNL Explain how the proposed research connects to one or more of PNNL s mission areas, including scientific discovery, energy resiliency, data science and computing, or national security. Clearly Explain the Research Impact Applicants should make it clear why the proposed research matters and what could change if the research is successful. Present a Strong Research Plan The proposal should provide a logical pathway from the research question to the anticipated outcomes. Demonstrate Independence The fellowship is an opportunity to establish an independent research identity. Applicants should demonstrate their ability to formulate and lead an ambitious research programme. Review Eligibility Carefully Candidates should confirm that their PhD timing, academic field, work authorisation, and other requirements satisfy the official fellowship conditions before submitting an application. Important Information for Applicants Applicants should rely on the official PNNL fellowship and careers pages for the most current requirements. The opportunity is highly competitive, and meeting the basic eligibility requirements does not guarantee selection. Candidates should also ensure that their proposal and supporting materials accurately represent their academic background, research achievements, and proposed work. Conclusion The Linus Pauling Distinguished Postdoctoral Fellowship 2027 offers an exceptional opportunity for recent and upcoming PhD graduates in science and engineering to pursue ambitious independent research at the Pacific Northwest National Laboratory in the United States. Selected fellows receive full funding to undertake a major research project of their own conception while benefiting from mentorship by internationally recognised researchers and access to PNNL s advanced scientific capabilities. With research opportunities spanning Scientific Discovery, Energy Resiliency, Data Science and Computing, and National Security , the fellowship is particularly suited to researchers with innovative ideas and the ambition to make significant contributions to their fields. Qualified candidates should begin preparing their research proposal and supporting application materials early. Applications close on 15 October 2026 at 4:00 p.m. PST . title: Mitacs Globalink Research Award 2026: Up to $12,000 for International Research Internships in Canada and Eligible Countries
summary: The Mitacs Globalink Research Award (GRA) provides an opportunity for senior undergraduate students, graduate students, and postdoctoral fellows to participate in international research collaborations between Canada and eligible countries and regions. Through the program, successful applicants can undertake a research internship under the joint supervision of a home-country and host-country professor, gaining international research experience while developing academic and professional connections across borders. The program supports research projects lasting between 12 and 24 weeks for one internship unit , while applicants receiving two internship units can undertake a longer research period or complete two separate research projects, subject to the program s rules. For students and postdoctoral researchers interested in international academic collaboration, this program can provide access to research environments outside their home institution, international academic networks, and financial support toward eligible project-related costs. What Is the Mitacs Globalink Research Award? The Mitacs Globalink Research Award is designed to facilitate international research collaboration and academic mobility . It brings together researchers from eligible Canadian and international institutions so that interns can conduct research in another country under the supervision of academic researchers. Successful applicants work under the joint supervision of a home supervisor and a host supervisor . This structure allows participants to remain connected to their home institution while gaining experience conducting research in an international academic environment. The program is particularly relevant to students and postdoctoral fellows who already have a research direction and are able to identify suitable academic supervisors and an appropriate host institution. Mitacs Globalink Research Award Streams The program is offered through two principal streams. 1. Allocation Stream Under the Allocation Stream, participating Canadian universities receive a designated number of internship units each year. Each Canadian university manages its own allocation, meaning that rules, conditions, and availability may differ between institutions . Applicants are therefore encouraged to contact their local Mitacs Advisor before developing their project so they can determine whether the proposed research fits their institution s available allocation and requirements. 2. Quantum Stream The Quantum Stream is open to all Canadian universities . Unlike the Allocation Stream, there is no limit on the number of projects a Canadian university can submit through the Quantum Stream , and projects submitted under this stream do not count toward the university s regular internship allocation. Projects under the Quantum Stream must focus on the quantum sector. Areas mentioned by the program include: Quantum computation, including hardware Quantum algorithms Quantum software Quantum communication Quantum networks Quantum cryptography Quantum metrology Quantum sensing Quantum imaging Quantum materials Applicants whose research falls within the quantum field may therefore want to investigate the Quantum Stream separately when planning their application. How Much Funding Does the Mitacs Globalink Research Award Provide? The program provides $6,000 per internship unit . Depending on the number of internship units awarded, participants can receive either $6,000 or $12,000 in research award funding. One Internship Unit One internship unit provides: $6,000 research award One research project lasting 12 to 24 weeks Research conducted in the other country Two Internship Units Two internship units provide: $12,000 research award Either one research project lasting 24 to 48 weeks , or Two separate research projects, each lasting 12 to 24 weeks Awards are offered in partnership with Mitacs s Canadian academic institution partners and remain subject to available funding. Applicants should also be aware that the award may not necessarily cover every expense associated with international research travel. The program encourages applicants to seek additional sources of financial support and to use prudence when budgeting for travel and accommodation. What Can the Mitacs Funding Be Used For? Mitacs funding must be spent according to the budget included in the application and in accordance with eligible Tri-Agency expenses. The program s funding administration also allows funds to support eligible direct research costs and other approved project-related expenses. Following approval, Mitacs sends the funds to the Canadian institution s Office of Research Services or equivalent administrative office. The institution then administers the funding as a research grant in the Canadian supervisor s name. Potential applicants should therefore carefully review their university s policies regarding research expenditures and funding administration before finalizing their project budget. Additional International Partner Funding The program information also notes that some international partners may provide additional funding. However, such funding is outside Mitacs s purview . Applicants interested in partner-specific funding are expected to contact the relevant partner organization directly. The supplied program information identifies partner information for countries including India and South Korea . Who Can Apply for the Mitacs Globalink Research Award? The program is aimed at researchers at different stages of higher education and early research careers. Eligible interns include: Full-time senior undergraduate students Full-time graduate students Postdoctoral fellows Applicants must be registered at an eligible Canadian or eligible international institution and must remain registered in the relevant status throughout their Globalink Research Award. Postdoctoral Eligibility Postdoctoral fellows may apply when: Their PhD graduation date is no more than five years before the proposed research project start date ; and They hold postdoctoral status at an eligible institution. Other Important Applicant Requirements Applicants must also satisfy several additional conditions. They: Must not undertake their research project at an institution where they previously completed a degree. Cannot conduct the research project in a country where they hold citizenship. Must be at least 18 years old , meeting the legal age of majority requirement in Canada. Must meet travel requirements for their destination, including applicable visa, immigration, and documentation requirements. Cannot hold more than two Globalink Research Awards or Mitacs-JSPS Summer Program Awards during their academic lifetime. Cannot participate in more than one Mitacs internship simultaneously. There are also specific rules for Canadian citizens and permanent residents enrolled at institutions outside Canada, as well as Canadian-enrolled students who hold citizenship in an eligible country. Who Can Serve as a Supervisor? The program also establishes eligibility requirements for supervisors. A supervisor must: Hold a faculty position at an eligible university. Be eligible to supervise graduate students. For supervisors at Canadian institutions, be eligible to hold Tri-Agency funding. Applicants should therefore identify appropriate academic supervisors before progressing too far with their application. An important point is that Mitacs does not connect interested interns with academic supervisors . Participants are responsible for connecting with one another and discussing research interests. Which Countries Are Eligible? The Mitacs Globalink Research Award has broad international reach. According to the supplied program information, research and travel are supported between Canadian academic institutions and institutions in most countries , subject to the program s country and travel-advisory restrictions. For outbound mobility from Canada, applicants cannot travel to countries classified by the Government of Canada under the relevant “Avoid all travel” or “Avoid non-essential travel” categories. For inbound mobility to Canada, the program states that all countries are eligible except Russia and North Korea . Because travel advisories can change, applicants must verify the status of their intended destination both when submitting their application and before travelling. Is There a Specific Nationality or Race Requirement? The program information does not identify a race-based eligibility requirement . Eligibility is instead structured around factors such as: Citizenship and destination Enrollment at an eligible institution Academic status Institution eligibility Research project requirements Travel eligibility Supervisor eligibility Importantly, applicants generally cannot undertake their research project in a country where they hold citizenship . Therefore, applicants should assess their eligibility based on their institution, academic status, citizenship, intended research destination, and the specific mobility rules rather than assuming that the program is restricted to one nationality or continent. How to Apply for the Mitacs Globalink Research Award The application process can vary depending on the Canadian university and its available internship-unit allocation. Applicants should first contact their local Mitacs Advisor to determine whether their proposed project meets the funding requirements for their institution and to obtain the appropriate GRA Application Portal link. The program recommends applying at least 16 weeks before the planned project start date . The formal submission guidance also states that complete applications should be submitted 12–16 weeks before the project start date . Step 1: Review the Eligibility Requirements Applicants should carefully review both: Mitacs eligibility and award guidelines; and The requirements established by their Canadian institution. University-specific requirements can affect the application process, particularly for projects submitted through the Allocation Stream. Step 2: Identify and Connect With Supervisors Potential interns and supervisors need to connect with each other and discuss research interests and potential projects. Mitacs does not serve as a matchmaking service for interns and academic supervisors, so applicants should take responsibility for establishing the academic collaboration themselves. Step 3: Obtain Canadian University Endorsement For supervisors at Canadian institutions, the appropriate institutional endorsement must be obtained before the application is prepared. Applicants should contact their local Mitacs Advisor to understand the specific rules and internal process applicable at their Canadian university. Step 4: Prepare the Application Applicants must complete the required fields in the application portal. The application also requires: A research proposal A Mitacs Pre-Departure form Personal information from all participants Responses to a research security question Required participant sign-offs The research security question is visible only to the relevant participant, and each participant must personally log in and provide their response. Step 5: Obtain All Required Signatures Once the application is complete, all participants must log in again and sign off on the project. The Canadian university signature requirements depend on the stream. For the Allocation Stream , the project must count toward the university s internship allocation, and the Vice President Research or designate signature is required. For the Quantum Stream , projects do not count against the university s allocation and the Vice President Research or designate signature is not required. However, the Office of Research Services or its designate must provide a signature on completed applications from either stream. Applicants should allow approximately one to three weeks to obtain the appropriate university signatures. Step 6: Submit the Complete Application The complete application should be submitted 12–16 weeks before the intended project start date . Only certain participants are authorized to submit the application through the portal, including: Local Mitacs Advisors Academic supervisors at Canadian institutions The intern who created the application Once the application has been submitted, participants receive a confirmation email. Learn more HERE What Happens After You Apply? Applicants should understand that approval is not the only requirement before travelling. The program explicitly states that interns cannot travel until Mitacs has issued both an outcome and an award letter . If the application is approved: Funding is provided to support eligible travel and accommodation expenses, research-related expenses, and stipend. Funds are transferred to the Canadian institution s research administration office. The Canadian supervisor administers the funding as a research grant. The project must begin within one year of the outcome letter being issued. If a second internship unit is awarded, the project must end within two years of the start date of the first unit. Interns are generally expected not to leave the host country during an internship unit. All participants must complete an exit survey at the end of the project. FAQS HERE Mitacs Globalink Research Award Deadline The supplied program information does not provide a single fixed calendar deadline for the Globalink Research Award. Instead, applications are tied to the proposed research project start date. Applicants are advised to submit their complete application 12–16 weeks before the project begins , and the program recommends applying at least 16 weeks before the planned start date . This means applicants should not wait for a single annual deadline. Instead, they should plan backward from their intended project start date and allow sufficient time for: Finding a research supervisor Developing the project Preparing the research proposal Completing the application Obtaining institutional endorsement Securing university signatures Completing the submission process Receiving the Mitacs outcome and award letter Completing necessary travel and immigration arrangements Because institutional allocation and funding availability can affect the process, prospective applicants should contact their local Mitacs Advisor as early as possible. Important Things Applicants Should Know Before applying, prospective participants should pay attention to several important program conditions. Funding Is Subject to Availability The award is offered in partnership with Mitacs s Canadian academic institution partners and is subject to available funding. Applicants Need to Find Their Own Academic Collaboration Mitacs does not connect interns and supervisors. Applicants need to establish the appropriate academic relationship themselves. University Requirements Can Differ The application process can vary depending on the Canadian university and whether the project is being submitted through the Allocation or Quantum Stream. Travel Restrictions Matter Applicants must meet the travel, visa, immigration, and documentation requirements of their intended destination. They must also check current travel advisories because country eligibility can change. Do Not Travel Before Receiving the Required Approval An intern must wait until Mitacs has issued both an outcome and award letter before travelling for the project. Why This Opportunity Can Be Valuable for Researchers The Mitacs Globalink Research Award combines international mobility with academic research collaboration. For eligible students and postdoctoral fellows, the program can provide an opportunity to: Conduct research in another country Work under joint academic supervision Build international research relationships Gain experience in a different academic environment Develop a structured international research project Access up to $12,000 in award funding, depending on the number of internship units Participate in research collaborations involving Canadian and international institutions Develop experience that can strengthen an academic or research career The program is particularly relevant for applicants who already have a defined research interest and can identify appropriate home and host supervisors. Final Takeaway The Mitacs Globalink Research Award is an international research mobility opportunity connecting Canadian and international academic institutions. It supports eligible senior undergraduate students, graduate students, and postdoctoral fellows who want to undertake collaborative research abroad under the joint supervision of academic researchers. Funding can reach $12,000 , depending on whether an applicant receives one or two internship units, while research projects can range from 12 to 48 weeks depending on the structure of the award. There is no single fixed annual deadline stated in the supplied information. Instead, applicants should plan to submit their complete applications 12–16 weeks before the intended project start date , with Mitacs recommending that applicants begin the process at least 16 weeks ahead. Because university allocation, institutional procedures, funding availability, supervisor eligibility, and international travel rules can affect an application, prospective applicants should begin early and consult their local Mitacs Advisor before developing and submitting their project. For eligible researchers seeking international academic experience and collaborative research opportunities, the Mitacs Globalink Research Award can serve as a pathway to develop research projects across borders while building connections between Canadian and international academic communities. title: iDICE Skills Training to Jobs Programme 2026: 300,000 Free Training Opportunities for Nigerian Youth
summary: The Federal Government of Nigeria , through the Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises (iDICE) Programme , is rolling out the iDICE Skills Training to Jobs Programme , a nationwide initiative designed to equip young Nigerians with market-relevant digital and creative skills and connect trained participants to employment opportunities. The programme is being implemented across Nigeria s six geopolitical zones , covering the North West, North East, North Central, South West, South East, and South South regions. The iDICE programme is a Federal Government initiative implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI) to strengthen Nigeria s technology and creative sectors through skills development, enterprise support, access to finance, and ecosystem development. Official programme information confirms that iDICE targets young Nigerians aged 15 to 35 and is designed to improve employability, encourage innovation, and support entrepreneurship. What Is the iDICE Skills Training to Jobs Programme? The iDICE Skills Training to Jobs Programme is focused on preparing young Nigerians for opportunities in the growing digital services, outsourcing, technology, and creative economies. Rather than concentrating only on training, the programme is designed around a training-to-employment pathway . Participants are expected to develop practical, industry-relevant skills that can be applied in the workplace and the global digital services market. According to the programme announcement, the initiative will provide 300,000 free training places and has an 80% employment connection target , making job linkage a central component of the programme. The broader iDICE programme has identified skills and enterprise development as one of its major intervention areas, with the goal of creating a skilled talent pool that can be connected to employment or supported in establishing innovative enterprises. Key Highlights of the iDICE Skills Training to Jobs Programme The programme offers several important features for young Nigerians seeking to develop employable skills. 1. 300,000 Free Training Places One of the biggest features of the initiative is the availability of 300,000 training places . The training is offered free of charge , meaning eligible young Nigerians can participate without paying a training fee. This large-scale approach is intended to expand access to digital and creative skills development across Nigeria rather than limiting participation to a small number of beneficiaries. The Bank of Industry has separately described iDICE as a nationwide digital skills and enterprise programme targeting more than 300,000 Nigerians. 2. Training in Market-Relevant Digital and Creative Skills Participants will receive training designed around the demands of the digital economy and global outsourcing market. The BPO component of iDICE is specifically designed to prepare Nigerian youth for employment opportunities in the global digital services economy, including areas such as remote service delivery, digital customer support, business process outsourcing operations, and global freelancing. ( Idice ) This creates an opportunity for young people to develop skills that can be applied both locally and in internationally connected digital work environments. 3. Strong Focus on Job Linkage The programme goes beyond skills acquisition by incorporating employment connections. The announced programme has an 80% employment connection target , meaning the initiative is designed with a strong emphasis on helping trained participants move from learning into employment opportunities. This focus is particularly significant for young Nigerians who may already have some educational qualifications but lack practical, market-ready skills or direct access to employers. The broader iDICE programme similarly emphasises the connection between skills development and the job market. Its digital and creative hubs are intended to provide young people with employability skills and strengthen links between training institutions and employers. Nationwide Coverage Across Nigeria The iDICE Skills Training to Jobs Programme is being rolled out across all six geopolitical zones of Nigeria. These are: North West North East North Central South West South East South South This nationwide approach is intended to ensure that young people from different parts of Nigeria can access the programme. The wider iDICE programme is already operating across Nigeria s geopolitical zones, with BOI reporting that implementation activities were underway across all six zones as of June 2026. Who Can Apply? The programme is targeted at young Nigerians aged 15 to 35 . Official iDICE documentation confirms that the programme s skills component is designed for Nigerian nationals within this age range. The opportunity is therefore particularly relevant to young Nigerians who: Are between 15 and 35 years old Want to acquire digital or creative skills Are seeking employment opportunities Want to develop skills for remote or global digital work Are interested in the business process outsourcing sector Want to strengthen their employability Are interested in Nigeria s growing technology and creative economy May want to build a career in digital services, freelancing, or related industries The programme is intended for Nigerian nationals , rather than applicants from other countries. Female Participation The programme places specific emphasis on inclusive participation. At least 40% female participation is targeted under the announced Skills Training to Jobs initiative. This is intended to increase women s participation in digital skills development and the opportunities created by Nigeria s expanding technology and creative sectors. Gender inclusion is also consistent with the broader iDICE programme s focus on addressing gaps in women s access to STEM education, entrepreneurship, skills, and financing. Participation for Persons with Disabilities The programme also provides for 5% participation by persons with disabilities . This inclusion target is intended to ensure that people with disabilities can participate in the digital skills and employment opportunities being created through the initiative. The focus on inclusion means the programme is not simply designed to increase the number of people receiving training; it also seeks to ensure that women and persons with disabilities have meaningful access to the opportunities. What Is Business Process Outsourcing (BPO)? A major area connected to the iDICE Skills Training to Jobs Programme is Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) . BPO involves organisations outsourcing specific business functions or services to specialised workers or service providers. In a digital economy, BPO can include activities such as: Customer support Remote service delivery Administrative support Digital operations Business process management Virtual assistance Other technology-enabled services Nigeria has a large young population and an expanding technology ecosystem, making digital services and outsourcing important areas for employment and economic development. The iDICE BPO programme specifically aims to position Nigerian youth to participate in global digital services and outsourcing opportunities. How the Programme Fits Into the Wider iDICE Initiative The Skills Training to Jobs Programme is part of the broader Investment in Digital and Creative Enterprises (iDICE) initiative. iDICE is designed to strengthen Nigeria s technology and creative ecosystems through several interconnected interventions. These include: Skills and Enterprise Development This component focuses on: Digital and creative skills training Entrepreneurship development Incubation Mentorship Capacity building Connections between talent and industry Access to Finance The programme also supports technology and creative businesses through financing mechanisms. The iDICE ecosystem currently includes financing facilities for eligible technology and creative enterprises, include Ecosystem Development iDICE is also investing in infrastructure and partnerships that can support innovation and entrepreneurship. The programme is establishing and upgrading digital and creative hubs in Nigerian universities and polytechnics. BOI reported in June 2026 that work was underway on digital and creative hubs in 66 institutions across the country. These facilities are intended to support training, innovation, incubation, entrepreneurship, and connections between academia and industry. Why This Opportunity Matters Nigeria s technology and creative industries continue to create opportunities for people with relevant digital skills. However, having access to education does not always translate into employment. Many young people need practical skills, industry exposure, and connections to employers before they can successfully enter the labour market. The iDICE Skills Training to Jobs Programme addresses this challenge by combining: Free skills training Industry-relevant learning Digital and creative sector exposure Employment connections Nationwide access Inclusion of women Inclusion of persons with disabilities This training-to-employment model can provide a more direct pathway between acquiring skills and finding work. What Participants Can Gain By participating in the programme, eligible young Nigerians can potentially gain: Practical digital and creative skills Exposure to the global digital services economy Skills relevant to BPO and remote work Improved employability Access to employment connections Greater understanding of digital career opportunities Experience that can support future professional development Participants should note that training does not automatically guarantee employment. The programme s 80% employment connection target represents a programme objective rather than a promise that every participant will receive a job. Application Process Applications for the Skills Training to Jobs Programme are announced through the programme s designated application channels. The announcement provided for this opportunity states that applications are free and open . Applicants should use the official application link and provide accurate information during registration. How to Apply Visit the official application platform. Review the eligibility requirements. Complete the application form with accurate personal information. Submit the required information. Follow the instructions provided after submission. Monitor the official iDICE communication channels for updates regarding selection, training, and subsequent employment-linkage activities. Application Link: https://lnkd.in/eyPgP7gb Applicants should be cautious of anyone requesting payment in exchange for access to the free training programme. Is There an Application Deadline? No specific application deadline is stated in the programme announcement provided. The announcement says that applications are free and open now . Applicants should therefore apply through the designated application platform and monitor the official iDICE channels for any updates or changes to the application window. About the Organisations Supporting iDICE The iDICE programme is a Federal Government of Nigeria initiative implemented by the Bank of Industry (BOI) . The programme is supported through financing partnerships involving the African Development Bank (AfDB), Agence Française de Développement (AFD), Islamic Development Bank (IsDB), and Bank of Industry . Official BOI materials confirm the role of these development finance partners in the programme. ( BOI ) The programme s broader objective is to strengthen Nigeria s digital and creative economy by investing in people, businesses, infrastructure, and access to finance. Other Opportunities Under iDICE The Skills Training to Jobs initiative is only one part of the broader iDICE ecosystem. Other iDICE interventions include: Startup Bridge , which supports entrepreneurs at different stages of development BPO Training , focused on digital services and outsourcing Hackathons , which bring innovators together to solve technology-related problems Creathons , which focus on creative-sector innovation Innovation and Creativity Enterprise Centres , which support skills development and startup activities Financing facilities for eligible technology and creative enterprises The official iDICE platform provides information on active and upcoming opportunities under the programme. Apply only through the designated application channel. Do not pay anyone to submit an application on their behalf. Keep records of their application details. Monitor official iDICE and BOI channels for updates. Read all instructions carefully before submitting an application. Conclusion The iDICE Skills Training to Jobs Programme 2026 represents a major opportunity for young Nigerians to develop practical digital and creative skills and gain stronger connections to employment opportunities. With 300,000 free training places , nationwide coverage across all six geopolitical zones, an 80% employment connection target , and dedicated participation targets for women and persons with disabilities, the initiative is designed to make digital skills development more accessible to young Nigerians. The opportunity is particularly relevant to Nigerians aged 15 to 35 who want to build careers in digital services, BPO, creative industries, freelancing, and other areas of the modern digital economy. title: MSCA Doctoral Networks 2026: European Commission Funding for International PhD Training, Research and Doctoral Careers
summary: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Networks 2026 call offers an important opportunity for universities, research institutions, businesses, public organisations, NGOs and other eligible organisations to establish international doctoral training programmes and recruit doctoral candidates from around the world. Funded under Horizon Europe , MSCA Doctoral Networks are designed to develop the next generation of researchers through international, interdisciplinary and inter-sectoral research and training. The programme places strong emphasis on research excellence, transferable skills, innovation, entrepreneurship, career development, international mobility and collaboration between academic and non-academic sectors. The 2026 call opens on 28 May 2026 and closes on 24 November 2026 at 17:00 CET . Importantly, this is not a conventional individual PhD scholarship application in which a student applies directly to the European Commission. The Doctoral Networks call is primarily submitted by international consortia of eligible organisations that propose a doctoral training programme. Successful networks subsequently recruit doctoral candidates through open and merit-based vacancies. MSCA Doctoral Networks 2026 at a Glance Programme: Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Networks Call: MSCA Doctoral Networks 2026 Category: Doctoral research and fellowship funding Funding framework: Horizon Europe Application opening date: 28 May 2026 Application deadline: 24 November 2026 at 17:00 CET Applicants: International consortia of eligible organisations Doctoral candidates: Researchers from all nationalities, subject to the programme s eligibility requirements Fields: Various scientific and research disciplines Training models: Standard Doctoral Networks, Industrial Doctoral Networks and Joint Doctoral Networks Geographical scope: International, with participation rules depending on the status of participating countries under Horizon Europe Application platform: European Commission Funding Tenders Opportunities Portal What Are MSCA Doctoral Networks? The Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Networks are part of the European Union s MSCA programme, which focuses on developing research talent and strengthening research and innovation capacity. Doctoral Networks bring together organisations from different sectors and countries to create structured doctoral programmes. Rather than simply funding individual research projects, the programme supports networks that can provide doctoral researchers with: High-quality research training. International research experience. Interdisciplinary training. Exposure to different sectors. Transferable skills development. Entrepreneurial skills. Professional networking opportunities. Supervision and mentoring. Career development support. Opportunities to work with organisations outside academia. International mobility and secondments. Preparation for long-term careers inside and outside academia. The programme therefore seeks to produce researchers who are not only technically strong in their particular research fields but are also equipped with the broader skills required to succeed in today s research, innovation and professional environments. The Three Types of MSCA Doctoral Networks The 2026 call provides different models of Doctoral Networks. Applicants should determine which model best matches the objectives, structure and partnerships of their proposed doctoral programme. 1. Standard Doctoral Networks Standard Doctoral Networks promote international, interdisciplinary and inter-sectoral cooperation for the training of PhD candidates across different scientific areas. The model is designed to help researchers develop: Research expertise. Transferable skills. Entrepreneurial mindsets. Research-related competencies. International experience. Interdisciplinary perspectives. Long-term career prospects. Standard Doctoral Networks can be particularly valuable where several institutions and sectors need to work together to provide doctoral researchers with a broad training environment. 2. Industrial Doctoral Networks Industrial Doctoral Networks are designed to strengthen the connection between academia and industry . Doctoral candidates receive training that includes exposure to skills and environments outside academia. The programme also supports collaboration between academic and non-academic organisations. A major feature of Industrial Doctorates is joint supervision between industry and academia . This approach allows doctoral researchers to: Conduct advanced research. Gain experience outside traditional academic environments. Develop industry-relevant skills. Understand how research can be translated into practical applications. Build professional networks. Improve their employability beyond academia. Develop an innovation-oriented mindset. Industrial Doctoral Networks can therefore be particularly relevant to research areas where collaboration between universities, companies, businesses and other non-academic organisations can generate practical impact. 3. Joint Doctoral Networks Joint Doctoral Networks support integrated doctoral programmes that lead to joint or multiple doctoral degrees . These networks require deeper institutional collaboration and a joint governance structure. The participating institutions must establish joint procedures covering areas such as: Recruitment. Admission. Supervision. Evaluation. Doctoral training. Governance. Degree arrangements. For Joint Doctorates, at least three independent legal entities within the consortium must be entitled to award doctoral degrees. At least one institution conferring the joint, double or multiple doctoral degree must be established in an EU Member State and/or a Horizon Europe Associated Country. Learn More HERE Who Can Apply for MSCA Doctoral Networks 2026? The main applicants are organisations rather than individual doctoral students . Doctoral Networks are open to international consortia involving organisations from different socioeconomic sectors. Eligible types of organisations can include: Higher education institutions. Universities. Research institutions. Research infrastructures. Private-sector organisations. Industry. Businesses. Small and medium-sized enterprises. Public-sector organisations. National governments. Regional governments. Local governments. Government agencies. Museums. Non-governmental organisations. Think tanks. Charities. Other socioeconomic actors. This broad eligibility structure allows doctoral programmes to bring together different perspectives and expertise. Consortium Requirements A consortium applying for a Doctoral Network must meet specific requirements. The minimum consortium must include at least three independent legal entities . These entities must: Be established in different EU Member States or Horizon Europe Associated Countries. Include at least one organisation established in an EU Member State. Beyond this minimum requirement, organisations from other countries around the world may also participate as beneficiaries or associated partners, depending on the applicable country-status rules. This international structure is fundamental to the programme because MSCA Doctoral Networks are designed to promote cross-border research collaboration. Special Requirements for Joint Doctorates Joint Doctoral Networks have additional requirements. At least three independent legal entities in the consortium must be entitled to award doctoral degrees. Furthermore, at least one institution responsible for conferring a joint, double or multiple doctoral degree must be established in: An EU Member State; and/or A Horizon Europe Associated Country. These requirements are intended to ensure that Joint Doctoral Networks have the appropriate institutional capacity and degree-awarding arrangements. What Responsibilities Do Beneficiaries Have? All beneficiaries participating in the network must recruit at least one doctoral candidate . They must also provide appropriate arrangements for: Hosting recruited researchers at their premises. Supervising doctoral candidates. Providing research training. Supporting career development. Participating in network activities. Where appropriate, beneficiaries may use associated partners linked to them to host and supervise researchers. This means organisations should not join a consortium simply as passive partners. They need to have a meaningful role in implementing the doctoral programme. Can Organisations from Developing Countries Apply? Yes. Organisations based in low- and middle-income countries can also participate and may receive EU funding, subject to the specific conditions established under the MSCA Work Programme. Organisations should therefore carefully check the applicable country participation rules before assuming that their location automatically makes them eligible or ineligible. The Horizon Europe participating-country documentation should be consulted to determine the precise status of a country. Organisations participating in an EU-funded programme for the first time will also need to register and obtain a Participant Identification Code (PIC) . Who Can Be Recruited as a Doctoral Candidate? Doctoral candidates funded through MSCA Doctoral Networks must meet specific eligibility conditions. They: Must not already hold a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment . Can be of any nationality . Should be enrolled in a doctoral programme leading to a doctoral degree in at least one EU Member State or Horizon Europe Associated Country. May, under the programme s rules, be recruited through a beneficiary based in a non-EU, non-Associated third country in certain degree-awarding arrangements. Are normally employed for a period of at least 3 months and up to 36 months . May be employed for up to 48 months in the case of Joint Doctorates . Must comply with the applicable MSCA mobility rule. The programme therefore provides an international pathway for researchers who are beginning their doctoral careers and have not yet obtained a PhD or equivalent doctoral degree. The MSCA Mobility Rule One of the most important eligibility requirements for doctoral candidates is the mobility rule . In general, a researcher must not have: Resided in the country of the recruiting organisation; or Carried out their main activity there, such as work or studies, for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately before their recruitment date . This requirement is important because international mobility is a central component of MSCA programmes. Prospective doctoral candidates should therefore carefully examine their residence, study and employment history before applying for a specific doctoral vacancy. Additional Requirement for Industrial Doctorates Researchers recruited under Industrial Doctorates must spend at least 50% of their time outside academia . This requirement reflects the purpose of Industrial Doctoral Networks, which is to expose researchers to both academic and non-academic environments. The arrangement enables researchers to gain practical experience and develop skills relevant to careers in industry, business and other non-academic settings. How Long Can Researchers Be Employed? The standard employment period for researchers in Doctoral Networks is: Minimum: 3 months. Maximum: 36 months. Joint Doctorates: Up to 48 months. Researchers may also undertake secondments as part of their research training. In general, secondments can take place for up to half of the duration of their MSCA fellowship. However, this limitation does not apply in the same way to Industrial Doctorates and Joint Doctorates. What Are the Benefits of MSCA Doctoral Networks? MSCA Doctoral Networks offer extensive academic, professional and international development opportunities. International Research Experience Researchers become part of international networks involving organisations from multiple countries. This can provide valuable exposure to different research cultures, methodologies and professional environments. Interdisciplinary Training Doctoral candidates can work across disciplinary boundaries and learn how different research fields contribute to solving complex problems. Research Skills Development The programme supports researchers in developing advanced research competencies relevant to their doctoral projects. Transferable Skills Training extends beyond technical research skills. Researchers can develop competencies that may include: Communication. Project management. Entrepreneurship. Innovation. Collaboration. Networking. Research dissemination. Career planning. Exposure to Non-Academic Careers The programme places considerable emphasis on employability and career development. Researchers can gain exposure to: Industry. Businesses. SMEs. Public-sector organisations. NGOs. Other non-academic environments. This can help researchers understand career opportunities beyond traditional academic positions. International Mobility The programme encourages researchers to work and train across different countries and institutions. This international experience can strengthen both academic and professional development. Supervision and Mentoring Doctoral Networks place particular attention on the quality of supervision and mentoring. Industrial and Joint Doctorates also require joint supervision arrangements. Career Development Every recruited doctoral candidate should have a career development plan prepared jointly with their supervisor. The plan considers the researcher s: Research objectives. Training needs. Career needs. Teaching opportunities. Publication planning. Conference participation. Other relevant professional development activities. Research and Training Activities Successful Doctoral Networks are expected to provide comprehensive training environments. Researchers should have opportunities to: Acquire new research skills. Develop transferable competencies. Develop entrepreneurial abilities. Participate in interdisciplinary research. Work with academic and non-academic organisations where appropriate. Build professional networks. Exchange knowledge. Develop good scientific practices. Strengthen research integrity. Explore innovation and entrepreneurship. The network should make use of the complementary strengths of its participating organisations. Supervisory Board Each MSCA Doctoral Network should have a clearly identified Supervisory Board . The board plays an important role in coordinating network-wide: Training. Research activities. Supervision. Communication. Exchange of good practices. A strong supervisory structure can help ensure consistency and quality across the participating organisations. Recruitment of Doctoral Researchers MSCA Doctoral Networks are expected to recruit researchers through an open, transparent and merit-based process . Selected projects must advertise doctoral vacancies as widely as possible. This includes publication through the EURAXESS Jobs Portal , alongside other relevant networks and communication channels. Doctoral candidates can therefore be recruited from around the world, subject to the programme s eligibility requirements. Career Development and Employability Career development is a central element of the programme. Doctoral training is not limited to completing a research thesis. Networks are expected to help researchers prepare for their longer-term careers by providing opportunities for: Training. Teaching. Research dissemination. Conferences. Networking. Publication planning. Professional development. Exposure to potential employers. Engagement with society and citizens. The overall objective is to improve researchers employability and career prospects both within and beyond academia. Green Research and Sustainability MSCA Doctoral Networks also incorporate sustainability considerations. Projects are strongly encouraged to adopt environmentally sustainable practices in line with the MSCA Green Charter . Networks should report on their sustainability efforts. Sustainability may also be considered when distinguishing between otherwise equally ranked proposals. Applicants should therefore consider how sustainable research and project-management practices can be incorporated into their proposed network. Learn More HERE How to Prepare a Strong MSCA Doctoral Networks Application The European Commission outlines six key steps for organisations preparing a Doctoral Networks proposal. Step 1: Understand How the Funding Works Before developing a proposal, applicants should become familiar with: The Doctoral Networks scheme. The MSCA Work Programme. The relevant annexes. Funding rules. Eligibility requirements. Evaluation criteria. Different Doctoral Network modalities. The Funding and Tenders Opportunities Portal is a central resource for prospective applicants. The official Guide for Applicants, FAQs, proposal templates, application forms and evaluation documents should be reviewed carefully. Applicants can also participate in information sessions and workshops. Step 2: Confirm Consortium Eligibility Before investing significant time in proposal development, organisations should confirm that their consortium satisfies the minimum eligibility requirements. This includes checking: Number of participating legal entities. Independence of organisations. Countries where organisations are established. EU Member State participation. Degree-awarding requirements for Joint Doctorates. Recruitment responsibilities. Funding eligibility of participating organisations. Organisations uncertain about their eligibility can seek guidance from their MSCA National Contact Point . Step 3: Find the Right Partners A successful proposal requires a strong international and diverse consortium. Potential coordinators and partners can begin by examining existing institutional relationships. They can also use the opportunity to establish new partnerships with organisations in Europe and elsewhere. Useful partner-search resources include: MSCA Matchmaking. Funding and Tenders Opportunities Portal. European Enterprise Network. MSCA National Contact Points. For Industrial Doctoral Networks, organisations seeking stronger research-business collaboration can particularly benefit from contacting the European Enterprise Network. Step 4: Start Drafting the Proposal Once the consortium and project concept are established, applicants should begin drafting the proposal around the official award criteria and requirements. Applicants should carefully review: Award criteria. Budget structure. MSCA Financial Guide. Horizon Europe Programme Guide. Gender dimension and inclusiveness. Dissemination and exploitation. Open science. Research integrity. Intellectual property management. Communication and dissemination. The proposal should demonstrate not only strong research ideas but also the quality of the training environment, supervision, career development and collaboration arrangements. Step 5: Ask Others to Review the Proposal Applicants should not wait until the final days before asking for feedback. Draft proposals can be reviewed by: Colleagues. Institutional research-support teams. MSCA National Contact Points. Experienced researchers. Previous applicants. Peer review can help identify weaknesses, unclear sections, missing information and inconsistencies before submission Step 6: Submit the Application The MSCA Doctoral Networks 2026 call opens on 28 May 2026 . The application deadline is: 24 November 2026 at 17:00 CET. Applications must be submitted through the European Commission s Funding and Tenders Opportunities Portal . Applicants should become familiar with the Electronic Submission Service before the deadline. The European Commission strongly recommends submitting proposals well before the closing time to avoid last-minute technical or administrative problems. Proposals can be updated, downloaded or withdrawn up until the deadline. Learn more and apply HERE Important Resources for Applicants Prospective applicants should use official resources when preparing their proposals. These include: MSCA Doctoral Networks programme information. MSCA Work Programme 2026–2027. General annexes. Guide for Applicants. Funding and Tenders Opportunities Portal. MSCA Financial Guide. Horizon Europe Programme Guide. Evaluation forms. MSCA National Contact Points. EURAXESS Worldwide. EURAXESS Jobs Portal. MSCA Matchmaking platform. European Enterprise Network. CORDIS database of previously funded projects. The European Commission also provides information sessions and other support opportunities for applicants. Where Can Applicants Find Examples of Previous Doctoral Networks? The CORDIS database , the European Commission s official database of EU-funded research projects, can be used to explore previously funded Doctoral Networks. Studying previously funded projects can help prospective applicants understand: The types of research areas supported. How international consortia are structured. How academic and non-academic organisations collaborate. How training programmes are designed. How networks integrate career development. How research and innovation objectives are presented. Applicants should use previous projects for understanding and inspiration while ensuring that their own proposal responds directly to the current call requirements. Application Deadline The MSCA Doctoral Networks 2026 application deadline is 24 November 2026 at 17:00 CET . The call opens on 28 May 2026 . Applicants are strongly encouraged to begin preparations early because building an international consortium, developing the research programme, preparing training plans and completing the proposal can require significant coordination. How to Apply for MSCA Doctoral Networks 2026 The MSCA Doctoral Networks 2026 call is submitted through the European Commission s Funding and Tenders Opportunities Portal. Apply through the Funding Tenders Opportunities Portal Prospective applicants should also consult the official MSCA Doctoral Networks guidance before beginning the submission process. MSCA Doctoral Networks official page The official MSCA page should be used to confirm the latest requirements, eligibility rules, programme conditions and supporting documents. Pro Tip for Applicants Start early and build the consortium before drafting the full proposal. A strong MSCA Doctoral Networks application requires more than an excellent research idea. Applicants should carefully match partners to the scientific objectives, training programme, supervision structure, international mobility, non-academic engagement and career-development goals. Reviewing the official Work Programme and Guide for Applicants early can help prevent eligibility and proposal-design problems later. Conclusion The MSCA Doctoral Networks 2026 call provides a major opportunity to develop international doctoral training programmes and strengthen research collaboration across Europe and the wider global research community. Its distinctive strength lies in combining doctoral research with international mobility, interdisciplinary training, transferable skills, industry and non-academic exposure, supervision, career development and networking . The programme supports three major models: Standard Doctoral Networks, Industrial Doctoral Networks and Joint Doctoral Networks , allowing consortia to select an approach that best fits their research and training objectives. For organisations, success begins with establishing an eligible and complementary international consortium, identifying a strong research and training concept, understanding the funding and evaluation requirements, and developing a proposal that demonstrates high-quality research, supervision, training and career development. For prospective doctoral researchers, the opportunity is particularly relevant because successful networks recruit doctoral candidates from around the world through open and merit-based processes. However, individual researchers do not submit the main Doctoral Networks proposal themselves; they normally apply for doctoral vacancies advertised by successful networks. With the 24 November 2026 at 17:00 CET deadline approaching, organisations interested in establishing a Doctoral Network should begin consortium building, partner identification, proposal development and internal review as early as possible.
